lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Hedged the bank's interest-rate risk on its fixed-rate bond holdings by buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
- Cut the monthly close from 8 working days to 5 by automating 30 reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Mapping 600 general-ledger accounts to a new chart of accounts, rebuilding the allocation rules and testing them against two prior closes, cut manual journal entries from 350 to 90 a month.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Trained 5 plant controllers on the new budgeting template and wrote its user guide.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Showed the share value fell from USD 50 to USD 40, a 25% drop, when the discount rate rose by 1 point.
- Raised the model's forecast accuracy by 12% across 10 years, from 70% to 82%, by adding rate-case timing.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Wrote onboarding notes on the fund's models for new analysts.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be removed for most US applications.
items.because: They do not help assess qualifications and may invite bias.

items.says: Put Stonebridge before Crescent Bank.
items.because: Employment should run most recent first.

items.says: Specify what the USD 600M measures.
items.because: It would make the scale credible.

items.says: Explain how the under-4% forecast error was measured.
items.because: It would make the accuracy credible.

items.says: Clarify whether the forecast directly informed the USD 40M repayment.
Add an outcome for the capital-plan work if one is known.
items.because: The bullet establishes consistency but not its consequence.

items.says: Fix the awkward “Mapping … cut” sentence structure and tense.
items.because: It sits awkwardly alongside the other past-tense bullets.

items.says: Clarify whether the mapping caused the drop in manual entries or was part of a broader change.
The FCFE valuation uses the wrong discount rate.
items.because: FCFE is ordinarily discounted at the cost of equity; WACC is ordinarily used with free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: Buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration would not hedge the stated interest-rate risk.
items.because: It would generally increase the bank’s exposure to rate changes in those holdings.

items.says: Explain how “no rise in early defaults” was assessed.
items.because: An observation period or cohort comparison would make the risk result supportable.

items.says: Change “Writes” to past tense.
items.because: The Crescent Bank role ended in 2022.

items.says: Make the valuation date clear.
Do not treat being within 6% of the market price as proof the valuation was accurate.
items.because: The comparison is context, not necessarily proof of accuracy.

items.says: The stated 25% drop is incorrect.
items.because: A fall from USD 50 to USD 40 is 20% of USD 50.

items.says: Check that “1 point” means one percentage point.
Check that the sensitivity figures come from the model.
Clarify what was forecast and what the 70% and 82% scores measure.
Clarify whether the accuracy result came from historical back-testing.
items.because: A ten-year future forecast cannot yet have measured accuracy.

items.says: The improvement is described as “12%” rather than 12 percentage points.
items.because: The stated scores rise from 70% to 82%.

items.says: Remove the FP&A support bullet unless the fund had an FP&A team and the contribution can be named.
items.because: It is generic and seems out of place in an investment-fund project.

items.says: Specify the benchmark if relevant and space permits.
Keep the onboarding-notes bullet only if there is room.
items.because: The analysis and reporting bullets are stronger.

items.says: Consider adding software actually used for automation, reporting, or modeling.
items.because: “Excel” alone undersells the technical work described above.

items.says: Check whether the ongoing project has substantive work since November 2024; otherwise give it an accurate end date.
